item: A language or date heal of a law article re-indexes the article it healed, in the same commit, at both sites that heal
summary: upsert_law_corpus_article cleared a poll date from published_at (and set the catalog language) on an unchanged-text article and committed, without indexing it again, so every mention kept the poll day in observed_on and the old language: the article sat in one period by its own clock (published_at or created_at) and in another by every reader of the mentions. The heal now goes through the one index_article hook (reindex_healed_article) and commits with it (a failed re-index rolls the heal back, where a separate commit would have left nothing to heal); the status stays unchanged and the result says healed and the mention count; a document with nothing to heal is not indexed again. An independent read found the second site: register_documents (every boot and unlock through the law catalogue seed, and POST /api/law/seed) set Article.language and committed with no re-index, and runs before any corpus sync, so the corpus heal never saw a difference to heal. It now re-indexes each article whose language it set (after its own commit, a failure is logged and never breaks the boot) and bumps the corpus epoch once. Both sites bump the epoch (corpus_epoch) because the in-place rewrite of mention rows is invisible to the columnar rollup's id-watermark merge. Seven tests, mutants for always-index, commit-first, no re-index in the catalogue heal and no epoch bump die. Stated limits: the content-changed branch still commits before it indexes and bumps no epoch for its re-index; the corpus heal bumps once per healed document (an extra bump only forces a rebuild); a failed re-index at the catalogue site is logged and never repeated by itself, because the document row already states the language; the re-index is additive for the When-axis date tags, so tags resolved against the old poll date survive (measured); a failed re-index is repeated by the next CALL of the upsert, and sync_watched_laws has no production caller, so in production by the next text change; a store healed before this change keeps its stale stamps until the article is re-indexed. Two stale comments that said the heal does not re-index are reworded.
